crime_highlights: the protracted nature of the attack and the beating
the attack was done by four persons on one victim who was essentially defenceless
they broke down the hotel door, dragged Willcocks out of bed and out of the hotel to the waiting van, and gratuitously beat up the roommate
the parties stopped and obtained bear mace
rationale_highlights: the aboriginal backgrounds of these four accused still must be considered in fixing fit and proper sentences for each of them
the mitigating factors which, to some extent, must be taken into account
coupled with their aboriginal heritage and the fact that their developmental history appears to some extent in each case to have been affected by their upbringing
note: Victim's death only in long quoted para 7; crime passage uses court's summary.

crime_highlights: Toby Daniel Baptiste is before me for sentencing following upon his conviction on a single count of breaking and entering a dwelling place
Mr. Baptiste, in a state of insobriety, entered into the residence of a resident on the Sunshine Coast near Sechelt, British Columbia, uninvited
his lengthy record, which, depending on how one counts and what one counts, portrays either 12 or 17 offences of a similar kind
rationale_highlights: undoubtedly some substance to the claim in this case
Mr. Baptiste's father was a resident at a residential school
I am required and indeed think it appropriate to consider the direction in 718.2, which is that I take into account Mr. Baptiste's circumstances as a member of the aboriginal community
note: Court says it takes factor into account but never states its effect.

crime_highlights: Of the three, this offender was the most highly intoxicated
The offender was driving his motor vehicle
It left the travelled surface of the roadway at not less than 70 kilometres per hour, which was an excessive speed in the circumstances, and collided with a utility pole
The collision tore the car apart like a sardine can
the other two young people, the occupants, were fatally injured
rationale_highlights: I see nothing in any of the material I have read from his background or his aboriginal heritage that would explain why a disposition involving him should be any different than any other drunken driver
He is of an aboriginal background
note: Court finds heritage does not explain offence; lists it only as mitigating; residential school history in para 12.
